text:
Marathon Petroleum has fallen 1.2% today and 18.5% over two weeks as crude oil prices have weakened and refinery margins have compressed. US oil has dropped from the mid-$140s range (implied by the stock's peak price relative to historical correlations) to $99.64 per barrel—a sharp decline that directly cuts into what refiners can earn by processing crude into gasoline and diesel. At the same time, US storage inventories remain elevated (gasoline stocks especially), which signals weak demand and further pressures the price refiners can charge for finished products.

The near-term headwinds are real, but they may be temporary. Marathon announced a $4.2 billion asset sale and a strategic pivot to focus on Gulf Coast refining with higher-value diesel and export-grade gasoline—assets that should benefit when crude prices stabilize and global demand tightens inventory levels. For now, though, the market is punishing the stock on the immediate margin squeeze, not rewarding the longer-term positioning.
